pages.note: The head of the sheet: item 12 in two paragraphs — three sentences set flush, then one indented paragraph of heart-syllable material. PROSE throughout, wrapping at the measure, read from two 1.5x crops. Item 12 is the last item, and the chant ENDS here.

Beneath item 12 and separated by white space: a CENTRED heading in capitals, VIPASSIT, with a single centred line under it. Structurally the same shape as the title on page 312, so it is entered as its own chant rather than folded into the one above. It starts and ends here, and page 317 opens the Mahāsamaya Sutta.

verses.pali_roman: namobuddhassa dukkhaṃ aniccaṃ anattā rūpakhandho vedanākhandho saññākhandho saṅkhārakhandho viññāṇakhandho namo itipi so bhagavā.
verses.english: Homage to the Buddha. Suffering, impermanent, not-self: the aggregates of form, feeling, perception, formations and consciousness. Homage — such is the Blessed One.

verses.pali_roman: namodhammassa dukkhaṃ aniccaṃ anattā rūpakhandho vedanākhandho saññākhandho saṅkhārakhandho viññāṇakhandho namo svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo.
verses.english: Homage to the Dhamma. Suffering, impermanent, not-self: the aggregates of form, feeling, perception, formations and consciousness. Homage — well proclaimed by the Blessed One is the Dhamma.

verses.pali_roman: namosaṅghassa dukkhaṃ aniccaṃ anattā rūpakhandho vedanākhandho saññākhandho saṅkhārakhandho viññāṇakhandho namo supatipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho vāhaparittaṃ.
verses.english: Homage to the Saṅgha. Suffering, impermanent, not-self: the aggregates of form, feeling, perception, formations and consciousness. Homage — of good practice is the Blessed One's community of disciples. The protective recitation.

verses.pali_roman: namobuddhāya ma-a-u dukkhaṃ aniccaṃ anattā yāvatassa hāyo mona u-a-ma dukkhaṃ aniccaṃ anattā u-a-ma-a vandā namobuddhāya na-a kati nissaraṇa ārapakhuddhaṃ ma-a-u dukkhaṃ aniccaṃ anattā.
verses.english: Homage to the Buddha — ma-a-u — suffering, impermanent, not-self; and so on through the heart syllables u-a-ma and na-a, with reverence, escape, and again: suffering, impermanent, not-self.

vocabulary.meaning: the protective recitation — the word that closes item 12's third sentence and, with it, the numbered series
heart syllables again, as in item 9. Each letter stands for a phrase, so they are abbreviations rather than words and cannot be translated one by one

checks.issue: ANOTHER WORD BROKEN ACROSS A LINE END WITH NO HYPHEN — line 3 ends 'saññā' and line 4 opens 'khandho', for saññākhandho. That is the FOURTH unhyphenated break in this chant after the three on page 315, so it is this section's habit rather than an accident. Rejoined.
THE BOOK PRINTS 'supatipanno' where the standard form is suppaṭipanno — single p, and a plain t with no retroflex dot. Read at 5x on the crop. Kept as printed, NOT corrected.

Item 12 gives the same five khandhas three times over, once under each of the Three Refuges, and the three sentences are identical but for their opening and closing clause. That is the book's own structure and is not duplication to be collapsed.

checks.issue: ⚠ ENTERED AS ITS OWN CHANT, AND THAT IS A JUDGEMENT RATHER THAN A CERTAINTY. VIPASSIT is centred, in capitals, with white space above it and a single centred line below — structurally identical to how YOD PHRAKANTRAIPIDOK is set on page 312, which is why it is treated as a title. But it carries no bracketed English gloss as that title does, and it could instead be a closing label belonging to the chant above. Worth settling with the book in hand; if it is a closing, this chant should be folded into yod-phrakantraipidok as a closing rather than left standing.

The line is set tight enough to read as one word at page zoom — sabbadukkhāsabbabhayāsabbarogāvinassantu. Divided on the same measured basis as the rest of the section, and here the words are ordinary Pali so the division is not in doubt.

batch_status.notes: THIS COMPLETES YOD PHRAKANTRAIPIDOK and closes the stretch 312-316, which now joins the Mahāsamaya Sutta at 317. Two findings. (1) A FOURTH UNHYPHENATED LINE BREAK — saññā/khandho — after three on page 315. Four in two sheets makes it this section's habit, not an accident, and it is the fault most likely to survive unnoticed because it leaves no mark. (2) ⚠ VIPASSIT IS ENTERED AS ITS OWN CHANT ON A JUDGEMENT. It is set exactly like the page-312 title — centred, capitalised, white space above — but carries no English gloss as that one does, and it could be a closing label for the chant above instead. That is the one open question on this sheet and it needs the book.
